title: Cutting Tailored Clothing for Every Build
excerpt: Fit rules aren't one-size-fits-all advice — they change depending on your frame. Here's how we adjust for different builds.
author: Lipek Fashion Team
body: For a taller, leaner frame, we often add slightly more room through the chest and taper more aggressively at the waist to avoid a boxy silhouette that can look shapeless on longer proportions.
For a broader or more athletic build, jacket length and lapel width are adjusted together — a lapel that's too narrow can make broad shoulders look disproportionate.
For a shorter frame, we shorten the jacket length slightly and raise the button stance, which elongates the leg line visually without changing your actual proportions.
None of these are fixed formulas — they're starting points we adjust at your fitting based on how the garment actually sits on you, not a chart.
